chunks: My father (peace be upon him) narrated: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from al-Hakam ibn Miskin, from Umm Saeed al-Ahmasiyyah,

She said: I came to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and entered, and the maid came and said, 'I have brought the mount for you.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'O Umm Saeed, what is this mount for? Where are you going?' She said, 'I said, to visit the graves of the martyrs.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Tell me, what is surprising about you people of Iraq is that you travel from a long distance to visit the martyrs, but you leave the Chief of the Martyrs and do not visit him.' She said, 'I asked him, who is the Chief of the Martyrs?' He said, 'Al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him).' She said, 'I said, I am a woman.' He said, 'There is no harm for one like you to go to him and visit him.'
She said, 'What is for us in his visit?' He said, 'It equals one Hajj and one Umrah, and the I'tikaf of two months in the Sacred Mosque, and fasting for those two months.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting the grave of Imam Husayn (a.s.) according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the unique spiritual status of Imam Husayn (a.s.) as the 'Chief of Martyrs' (Sayyid al-Shuhada), urging believers not to overlook his grave while visiting other martyrs. The Imam’s specific validation for women underscores the inclusivity of Ziyarat, while the immense reward—equivalent to Hajj, Umrah, and two months of I'tikaf with fasting—reflects the theological weight of his sacrifice in Shia tradition.
